subjectOf.text: The design binds in one file, frozen by hash only after twenty-two rounds of blind audit by two model engines, and every harness and analysis step refuses to run against a design whose hash differs.
subjectOf.abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518
scope_conditions: Every random draw derives from a named hash template, so no draw depends on anything outside its listed fields.
The auditing engines are model engines and are not independent peer review.

subjectOf.text: In the final audit rounds of the last three sections of the working draft, one audit family's command-line engines returned no verdict because their usage balance was exhausted, so those rounds hold two passing verdicts rather than three and left identified low-severity findings unadopted.

scope_conditions: The shortfall is disclosed in the paper's own limits section and in the audit records.
It concerns the conduct of the study's review, not the filter's performance.
